title.zh: 卷二百五十六 列傳第十五 趙普弟:安易
title.en: Volume 256 Biographies 15: Zhao Pudi and Younger Brother: Anyi
title.raw: 卷二百五十六 列傳第十五 趙普弟:安易 Volume 256 Biographies 15: Zhao Pudi and Younger Brother: Anyi

sentences.zh: 趙普，字則平，幽州薊人。

translations.literal: Zhao Pu, style name Zeping, was a native of Ji in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu, whose style name was Zeping, came from Ji in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 後唐幽帥趙德鈞連年用兵，民力疲弊。

translations.literal: In the Later Tang, Zhao Dejun, military governor of You, waged war year after year, and the people's strength was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Tang, Zhao Dejun, military governor of You, fought year after year until the people were worn down and impoverished.

sentences.zh: 普父廻舉族徙常山，又徙河南洛陽。

translations.literal: Pu's father Hui moved the whole clan to Changshan, and then again to Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's father Hui relocated the entire clan first to Changshan and then to Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 普沈厚寡言，鎮陽豪族魏氏以女妻之。

translations.literal: Pu was deep and steady and sparing of speech; the powerful Wei clan of Zhenyang gave him their daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was grave, steady, and taciturn; the prominent Wei clan of Zhenyang married a daughter to him.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，永興軍節度劉詞辟為從事，詞卒，遺表薦普於朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande of Zhou, Liu Ci, military commissioner of Yongxing Circuit, recruited him as a staff member; when Ci died, his final memorial recommended Pu to the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xiande era of Zhou, Liu Ci, military commissioner of Yongxing Circuit, took him on as a staff officer; when Liu Ci died, his death memorial recommended Pu to the throne.

sentences.zh: 世宗用兵淮上，太祖拔滁州，宰相范質奏普為軍事判官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong campaigned on the Huai, Taizu captured Chuzhou, and Grand Councillor Fan Zhi memorialized to appoint Pu military affairs adjudicator.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Shizong was campaigning on the Huai, Taizu took Chuzhou, and Grand Councillor Fan Zhi recommended Pu for the post of military affairs adjudicator.

sentences.zh: 宣祖臥疾滁州，普朝夕奉藥餌，宣祖由是待以宗分。

translations.literal: When Xuanzu lay ill at Chuzhou, Pu attended him morning and evening with medicines; Xuanzu therefore treated him with the closeness of kin.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzu fell ill at Chuzhou, Pu brought him medicines morning and evening; Xuanzu thereafter treated him as one of the family.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗與語，奇之。

translations.literal: Taizu once spoke with him and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once conversed with him and was struck by his ability.

sentences.zh: 時獲盜百餘，當棄市，普疑有無辜者，啟太祖訊鞫之，獲全活者眾。

translations.literal: At the time more than a hundred bandits had been captured and were to be executed in the marketplace; Pu suspected that some were innocent, and reported this to Taizu to have them interrogated, and many were spared and kept alive.
translations.idiomatic: When more than a hundred captured robbers were about to be executed in the marketplace, Pu suspected that some were innocent; he appealed to Taizu to have them questioned, and many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 淮南平，調補渭州軍事判官。

translations.literal: When the Huainan region was pacified, he was transferred and appointed military affairs adjudicator of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Huainan region was pacified, he was reassigned as military affairs adjudicator at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖領同州節度，辟為推官；

translations.literal: When Taizu held the Tongzhou military commission, he recruited Pu as investigating officer;
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu served as military commissioner of Tongzhou, he recruited Pu as investigating officer;

sentences.zh: 移鎮宋州，表為掌書記。

translations.literal: when he moved his headquarters to Songzhou, he memorialized to appoint Pu chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: when Taizu transferred his command to Songzhou, he recommended Pu as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 太祖北征至陳橋，被酒臥帳中，眾軍推戴，普與太宗排闥入告。

translations.literal: When Taizu marched north and reached Chen Bridge, he lay drunk in his tent; the troops acclaimed him, and Pu together with Taizong pushed open the tent flap and entered to report it.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched north to Chen Bridge and lay drunk in his tent while the army proclaimed him emperor, Pu and Taizong pushed open the tent flap to tell him.

sentences.zh: 太祖欠伸徐起，而眾軍擐甲露刃，喧擁麾下。

translations.literal: Taizu stretched and rose slowly, while the troops donned armor and bared their blades, clamoring and pressing around beneath his banner.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu stretched, rose slowly, and found the soldiers already in armor with naked blades, shouting and crowding beneath his standard.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，以佐命功，授右諫議大夫，充樞密直學士。

translations.literal: When he accepted the mandate, Pu, for his merit in founding the dynasty, was appointed Right Remonstrance Grandee and Hanlin Academician of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu accepted the throne, Pu was made Right Remonstrance Grandee and Hanlin Academician of the Privy Council for his founding service.

sentences.zh: 車駕征李筠，命普與呂餘慶留京師，普願扈從，太祖笑曰：「若勝冑介乎？」

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Li Jun, he ordered Pu and Lü Yuqing to remain in the capital; Pu wished to accompany him, and Taizu smiled and said, "Do you plan to wear armor?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched against Li Jun, he left Pu and Lü Yuqing in the capital; Pu asked to accompany the campaign, and Taizu smiled and said, "Are you going to put on armor?

sentences.zh: 從平上黨，遷兵部侍郎、樞密副使，賜第一區。

translations.literal: After the pacification of Shangdang he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, and was granted one residence.
translations.idiomatic: After Shangdang was pacified, he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council and granted a residence.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，拜樞密使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong, he was appointed Commissioner of the Privy Council and Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong, he was made Commissioner of the Privy Council and Acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，范質等三相同日罷，以普為門下侍郎、平章事、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, Fan Zhi and the other three grand councillors resigned on the same day, and Pu was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery, Grand Councillor, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande, Fan Zhi and the other three chief ministers all resigned on the same day, and Pu was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery, Grand Councillor, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies.

sentences.zh: 中書無宰相署敕，普以為言，上曰：「卿但進敕，朕為卿署之可乎？」

translations.literal: In the Secretariat there was no chancellor's seal for edicts; Pu raised the matter, and the emperor said, "You need only submit the edict; shall I sign it for you?"
translations.idiomatic: Because the Secretariat had no chancellor's seal for issuing edicts, Pu raised the issue; the emperor said, "You need only draft the edict—shall I sign it for you?

sentences.zh: 普曰：「此有司職爾，非帝王事也。」

translations.literal: Pu said, "That is the duty of the proper office; it is not the business of an emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Pu replied, "That is the work of the proper office, not the business of an emperor.

sentences.zh: 令翰林學士講求故實，竇儀曰：「今皇弟尹開封，同平章事，即宰相任也。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Hanlin academicians to investigate precedent; Dou Yi said, "Now the emperor's younger brother, who governs Kaifeng as Grand Councillor, holds the office of chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Hanlin academicians to investigate precedent; Dou Yi said, "Your Majesty's younger brother, who governs Kaifeng as Grand Councillor, already holds the chancellor's role.

sentences.zh: 令署以賜普。

translations.literal: He ordered that the seal be signed and given to Pu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the seal signed and granted to Pu.

sentences.zh: 既拜相，上視如左右手，事無大小，悉咨決焉。

translations.literal: Once he had become chancellor, the emperor regarded him as his right and left hand; on matters great and small he consulted him and decided through him.
translations.idiomatic: Once appointed chancellor, he was treated by the emperor as indispensable; on matters large and small the emperor consulted him and deferred to his judgment.

sentences.zh: 是日，普兼監修國史。

translations.literal: On that day Pu was also appointed concurrently to supervise the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Pu was also made concurrent supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 命薛居正、呂餘慶參知政事以副之，不宣制，班在宰相後，不知印，不預奏事，不押班，但奉行制書而已。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Xue Juzheng and Lü Yuqing Vice Grand Councillors to assist him; their appointments were not proclaimed by edict, their court rank followed the chancellors, they did not hold the seal, did not participate in presenting memorials, did not lead the court assembly, but merely carried out imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Juzheng and Lü Yuqing were appointed Vice Grand Councillors to assist him without public proclamation; they ranked after the chancellors, held no seal, took no part in memorials or court assembly, and merely executed imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 先是，宰相兼敕，皆用內制，普相止用敕，非舊典也。

translations.literal: Previously, when chancellors concurrently issued edicts, they all used internal drafts; when Pu became chancellor he used only edicts—a departure from old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, chancellors who concurrently issued edicts had always used internal drafts; Pu as chancellor used only edicts, which was not the old practice.

sentences.zh: 太祖數微行過功臣家，普每退朝，不敢便衣冠。

translations.literal: Taizu often made incognito visits to the homes of his meritorious followers; whenever Pu withdrew from court he dared not immediately change out of his official dress.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu often visited his meritorious followers in disguise; after each court session Pu dared not change out of his official robes at once.

sentences.zh: 一日，大雪向夜，普意帝不出。

translations.literal: One day, heavy snow fell toward nightfall, and Pu thought the emperor would not go out.
translations.idiomatic: One day, as heavy snow fell toward evening, Pu assumed the emperor would not venture out.

sentences.zh: 久之，聞叩門聲，普亟出，帝立風雪中，普惶懼迎拜。

translations.literal: After a long while he heard knocking at the gate; Pu hurried out, and the emperor stood in the wind and snow; Pu, fearful, went forward to welcome him and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: After a long wait he heard a knock at the gate; he rushed out and found the emperor standing in the wind and snow; Pu, alarmed, hurried forward to receive him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「已約晉王矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I have already arranged to meet the Prince of Jin."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have already arranged to meet the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 已而太宗至，設重裀地坐堂中，熾炭燒肉。

translations.literal: Soon Taizong arrived; they spread layered mats and sat on the floor in the hall, and burned charcoal to roast meat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Taizong arrived; they laid down layered mats and sat on the floor in the hall while charcoal fire roasted meat.

sentences.zh: 普妻行酒，帝以嫂呼之。

translations.literal: Pu's wife served wine, and the emperor addressed her as sister-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's wife poured wine, and the emperor called her sister-in-law.

sentences.zh: 因與普計下太原。

translations.literal: Thereupon they discussed with Pu the plan to take Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Then they discussed with Pu the plan to capture Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 普曰「太原當西北二面，太原既下，則我獨當之，不如姑俟削平諸國，則彈丸黑子之地，將安逃乎？」

translations.literal: Pu said, "Taiyuan faces us on the northwest; once Taiyuan falls we alone must bear the brunt—better to wait until the other states are reduced, and then what escape will that pellet-sized speck of territory have?"
translations.idiomatic: Pu said, "Taiyuan guards our northwest; if we take it now we alone must bear the frontier burden. Better to wait until the other states are subdued—then that tiny enclave will have nowhere to flee.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「吾意正如此，特試卿爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "My thought is exactly this; I was only testing you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "That is exactly what I think; I was only testing you.

sentences.zh: 五年春，加右僕射、昭文館大學士。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year he was promoted to Right Vice Director and Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year he was promoted to Right Vice Director and Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 俄丁內艱，詔起復視事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother; an edict ordered him to leave mourning and resume office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when he entered mourning for his mother, an edict ordered him to leave mourning and return to duty.

sentences.zh: 遂勸帝遣使分詣諸道，徵丁壯籍名送京師，以備守衛；

translations.literal: He then urged the emperor to dispatch envoys to each circuit to register able-bodied men and send them to the capital for guard duty;
translations.idiomatic: He then urged the emperor to send envoys to every circuit to register strong young men and send them to the capital for guard service;

sentences.zh: 諸州置通判，使主錢穀。

translations.literal: and to establish supervisory commissioners in the prefectures to manage finances and grain.
translations.idiomatic: and to establish supervisory commissioners in the prefectures to manage revenue and grain.

sentences.zh: 由是兵甲精銳，府為充實。

translations.literal: Thereby the army and armor were sharp and strong, and the treasury was full.
translations.idiomatic: As a result the army was well equipped and the treasury well stocked.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年冬，普嘗病，車駕幸中書。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Kaibao, when Pu fell ill, the emperor visited the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Kaibao, when Pu fell ill, the emperor visited the Secretariat in person.

sentences.zh: 三年春，又幸其第撫問之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year the emperor again visited his residence to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year the emperor again visited his home to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 賜賚加等。

translations.literal: Gifts and rewards were increased by one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial gifts and rewards were increased by one grade.

sentences.zh: 六年，帝又幸其第。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the emperor again visited his residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the emperor visited his residence again.

sentences.zh: 時錢王俶遣使致書於普，及海物十瓶，置於廡下。

translations.literal: At the time Qian Chu, King of Wuyue, had sent an envoy with a letter to Pu and ten jars of maritime goods, which were placed beneath the corridor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time King Qian Chu of Wuyue had sent an envoy with a letter to Pu and ten jars of maritime goods, set beneath the corridor.

sentences.zh: 會車駕至，倉卒不及屏，帝顧問何物，普以實對。

translations.literal: Just as the emperor arrived, there was no time to hide them in haste; the emperor looked and asked what they were, and Pu answered truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrived unexpectedly, there was no time to hide them; asked what they were, Pu told the truth.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「海物必佳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Maritime goods must be fine."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Sea goods must be excellent.

sentences.zh: 即命啟之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered them opened.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered them opened.

sentences.zh: 皆瓜子金也。

translations.literal: They were all melon-seed gold.
translations.idiomatic: Inside were melon-seed gold nuggets.

sentences.zh: 普惶恐頓首謝曰：「臣未發書，實不知。」

translations.literal: Pu, fearful, prostrated himself and apologized, saying, "Your servant had not yet opened the letter and truly did not know."
translations.idiomatic: Pu, terrified, kowtowed and said, "I had not yet opened the letter and truly did not know.

sentences.zh: 帝歎曰：「受之無妨，彼謂國家事皆由汝書生爾！」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said, "Accepting it does no harm—they think all affairs of state are decided by you, a mere scholar!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said, "There is no harm in accepting it—they think all affairs of state are decided by you, a mere scholar!

sentences.zh: 普為政頗專，廷臣多忌之。

translations.literal: In governing, Pu was quite autocratic, and many court officials resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Pu governed with considerable autocracy, and many at court resented him.

sentences.zh: 時官禁私販秦、隴大木，普嘗遣親吏詣市屋材，聯巨筏至京師治第，吏因之竊貨大木，冒稱普市貨，鬻都下，權三司使趙玭廉得之以聞。

translations.literal: At the time the government forbade private trafficking in timber from Qin and Long; Pu once sent a trusted clerk to the market to buy house timber, and great rafts were linked and brought to the capital to build his residence; the clerk thereby smuggled timber in the process, falsely claiming it was Pu's purchase, and sold it in the capital; Zhao Pin, commissioner of the three departments, investigated and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Private sale of timber from Qin and Long was forbidden; Pu sent a trusted clerk to buy building timber, and linked great rafts to bring it to the capital for his mansion; the clerk smuggled timber on the side, falsely claiming it was Pu's purchase, and sold it in the capital; Zhao Pin, commissioner of the three departments, investigated and reported it.

sentences.zh: 太祖大怒，促令追班，將下制逐普，賴王溥奏解之。

translations.literal: Taizu was greatly angered and urgently ordered Pu recalled to court, intending to issue an edict expelling him; he was spared through Wang Pu's memorial interceding.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was furious and urgently ordered Pu recalled to court, intending to issue an edict removing him; Wang Pu's memorial interceded and saved him.

sentences.zh: 故事，宰相、樞密使每候對長春殿，同止廬中；

translations.literal: By precedent, the chancellor and commissioner of the Privy Council, whenever they awaited audience at the Hall of Everlasting Spring, stayed together in the same lodge;
translations.idiomatic: By custom, whenever the chancellor and the Privy Council commissioner waited for audience at the Hall of Everlasting Spring, they lodged together;

sentences.zh: 上聞普子承宗娶樞密使李崇矩女，即令分異之。

translations.literal: when the emperor heard that Pu's son Chengzong had married the daughter of Privy Council Commissioner Li Chongju, he immediately ordered them separated.
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor learned that Pu's son Chengzong had married Privy Council Commissioner Li Chongju's daughter, he ordered them separated at once.

sentences.zh: 普又以隙地私易尚食蔬圃以廣其居，又營邸店規利。

translations.literal: Pu also privately exchanged vacant land for the Imperial Kitchen's vegetable garden to enlarge his residence, and also built inns and shops for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Pu also privately traded vacant land for the Imperial Kitchen's vegetable garden to expand his home, and built inns and shops for profit.

sentences.zh: 盧多遜為翰林學士，因召對屢攻其短。

translations.literal: Lu Duosun was a Hanlin academician and, whenever summoned to audience, repeatedly attacked Pu's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duosun, a Hanlin academician, seized every audience to attack Pu's failings.

sentences.zh: 會雷有鄰擊登聞鼓，訟堂後官胡贊、李可度受賕骫法及劉偉偽作攝牒得官，王洞嘗納賂可度，趙孚授西川官稱疾不上，皆普庇之。

translations.literal: At the same time Lei Youlin struck the drum for grievances, accusing the rear-hall officials Hu Zan and Li Kedu of taking bribes and bending the law, Liu Wei of forging an acting appointment to obtain office, Wang Dong of once bribing Kedu, and Zhao Fu of receiving a Sichuan appointment yet claiming illness and not reporting—all shielded by Pu.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Lei Youlin struck the grievance drum, accusing rear-hall officials Hu Zan and Li Kedu of bribery and perversion of law, Liu Wei of forging an acting appointment, Wang Dong of once bribing Kedu, and Zhao Fu of taking a Sichuan post yet claiming illness and not reporting—all under Pu's protection.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，下御史府按問，悉抵罪，以有鄰為秘書省正字。

translations.literal: Taizu was angry and sent the case to the censorate for investigation; all were convicted, and Youlin was made Correcting Editor in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was enraged and ordered the censorate to investigate; all were found guilty, and Youlin was made Correcting Editor in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 普恩益替，始詔參知政事與普更知印、押班、奏事，以分其權。

translations.literal: Pu's favor declined further; only then was it decreed that the Vice Grand Councillors should alternate with Pu in holding the seal, leading the assembly, and presenting memorials, to divide his power.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's influence waned further; only then was it decreed that the Vice Grand Councillors should share with Pu the seal, court assembly, and memorials, dividing his authority.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為河陽三城節度、檢校太傅、同平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as military commissioner of Heyang Three Cities, Acting Grand Tutor, and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was posted out as military commissioner of Heyang Three Cities, Acting Grand Tutor, and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初入朝，改太子少保，遷太子太保。

translations.literal: When Taiping Xingguo began and he entered court, he was changed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taiping Xingguo era he came to court and was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, then promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 頗為盧多遜所毀，奉朝請數年，鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: He was greatly slandered by Lu Duosun and for several years attended court without appointment, depressed and unable to realize his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duosun slandered him heavily; for years he held only court attendance without office, frustrated and unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 會柴禹錫、趙鎔等告秦王廷美驕恣，將有陰謀竊發。

translations.literal: At the time Chai Yuxi, Zhao Rong, and others reported that Prince Qin Tingmei was arrogant and willful and was plotting a secret rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Then Chai Yuxi, Zhao Rong, and others reported that Prince Qin Tingmei was arrogant and was plotting a secret uprising.

sentences.zh: 帝召問，普言願備樞軸以察姦變，退又上書，自陳預聞太祖、昭憲皇太后顧託之事，辭甚切至。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned and questioned him; Pu said he wished to take up a post at the pivot to watch for treachery, and after withdrawing submitted a memorial stating that he had beforehand heard of the entrustments of Taizu and Empress Dowager Zhaoxian—the language was very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned him; Pu said he wished to return to the center of power to detect treachery, then withdrew and submitted a memorial declaring he had long known of the deathbed entrustments of Taizu and Empress Dowager Zhaoxian—his words were deeply earnest.

sentences.zh: 太宗感悟，召見慰諭。

translations.literal: Taizong was moved and summoned him for consolation and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was deeply moved and summoned him to comfort and reassure him.

sentences.zh: 俄拜司徒兼侍中，封梁國公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Education and Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Minister of Education and Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 先是，秦王廷美班在宰相上，至是，以普勳舊，再登元輔，表乞居其下，從之。

translations.literal: Previously Prince Qin Tingmei had ranked above the chancellor; now, because Pu was an old merit-holder who again ascended to chief minister, he memorialized asking to rank below Tingmei, and the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Prince Qin Tingmei had ranked above the chancellor; now, as an old founding minister restored to high office, Pu asked to rank below him, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 及涪陵事敗，多遜南遷，皆普之力也。

translations.literal: When the Fuling affair failed, Duosun was banished south—all through Pu's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fuling affair collapsed, Duosun was exiled south—all owing to Pu's handiwork.

sentences.zh: 八年，出為武勝軍節度、檢校太尉兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was sent out as military commissioner of Wusheng Circuit, Acting Grand Commandant, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was posted out as military commissioner of Wusheng Circuit, Acting Grand Commandant, and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝作詩以餞之，普奉而泣曰：「陛下賜臣詩，當刻石，與臣朽骨同葬泉下。」

translations.literal: The emperor composed a poem to send him off; Pu received it in tears and said, "Your Majesty has bestowed a poem upon your servant; it should be carved in stone and buried with my decayed bones beneath the springs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote a farewell poem; Pu received it weeping and said, "Your Majesty's poem should be carved in stone and buried with my bones in the grave.

sentences.zh: 帝為之動容。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved by this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was visibly moved.

sentences.zh: 翌日，謂宰相曰：「普有功國家，朕昔與遊，今齒髮衰矣，不容煩以樞務，擇善地處之，因詩什以導意。

translations.literal: The next day he said to the chancellor, "Pu has served the state with merit; I once wandered with him, and now his teeth and hair are failing; I cannot burden him further with pivot affairs, so I chose a good post for him and used verse to convey my intent.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he told the chancellor, "Pu has merited the state; I once kept his company, and now he is old; I cannot burden him with central affairs, so I found him a good post and used a poem to express my meaning.

sentences.zh: 普感激泣下，朕亦為之墮淚。」

translations.literal: Pu was moved to tears in gratitude, and I too shed tears for him."
translations.idiomatic: Pu wept in gratitude, and I wept with him.

sentences.zh: 宋琪對曰：「昨日普至中書，執御詩涕泣，謂臣曰：『此生餘年，無階上答，庶希來世得效太馬力。』

translations.literal: Song Qi replied, "Yesterday Pu came to the Secretariat, held the imperial poem and wept, and said to me, 'In the years left to me I have no way to repay Your Majesty above; I can only hope in the next life to offer the strength of dog and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qi replied, "Yesterday Pu came to the Secretariat, clutching the imperial poem in tears, and told me, 'In what years remain I cannot repay Your Majesty in this life; I can only hope in the next to serve with the loyalty of dog and horse.

sentences.zh: 臣昨聞普言，今復聞宣諭，君臣始終之分，可謂兩全。」

translations.literal: Yesterday I heard Pu's words, and today I hear Your Majesty's pronouncement—the bond between ruler and minister from beginning to end may truly be called complete on both sides.'
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I heard Pu; today I hear Your Majesty's words—the full arc of loyalty between ruler and minister is truly fulfilled on both sides.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年春，大軍出討幽薊，久未班師，普手疏諫曰：

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Yongxi, when the great army marched out to attack You and Ji and long failed to return, Pu submitted a handwritten memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Yongxi, as the great army marched against You and Ji and long delayed its return, Pu submitted a handwritten remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 「伏睹今春出師，將以收復關外，屢聞克捷，深快輿情。

translations.literal: "I humbly observe that this spring's expedition was launched to recover the lands beyond the passes; repeated reports of victory have deeply pleased public sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly note that this spring's campaign was meant to recover the territory beyond the passes; repeated reports of victory have greatly heartened the people.

sentences.zh: 然晦朔屢更，薦臻炎夏，飛輓日繁，戰鬥未息，老師費財，誠無益也。

translations.literal: Yet the dark and bright moons have changed again and again, and midsummer has come; transport convoys grow daily more numerous, fighting has not ceased, the army is worn and funds exhausted—this truly brings no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet month after month has passed and midsummer has arrived; supply wagons multiply daily and battle continues unabated—the army grows weary and the treasury drained, to no real gain.

sentences.zh: 伏念陛下自翦平太原，懷徠閩、浙，混一諸夏，大振英聲，十年之間，遂臻廣濟。

translations.literal: I humbly recall that since Your Majesty cut down Taiyuan, embraced Min and Zhe, and unified the lands of Xia, your glorious renown has resounded greatly; within ten years you have reached broad relief and succor.
translations.idiomatic: I recall that since Your Majesty subdued Taiyuan, won over Min and Zhe, and unified the central lands, your fame has thundered abroad; within a decade you have brought wide relief to the realm.

sentences.zh: 遠人不服，自古聖王置之度外，何足介意。

translations.literal: That distant peoples do not submit—from antiquity sage kings have set this outside their concern; it is not worth troubling over.
translations.idiomatic: That distant peoples refuse submission is something sage kings since antiquity have placed beyond concern; it is not worth fretting over.

sentences.zh: 竊慮邪諂之輩，蒙蔽睿聰，致興無名之師，深蹈不測之地。

translations.literal: I privately fear that flatterers and sycophants have blinded Your Majesty's clear hearing and led you to raise an army without just cause and plunge deep into unpredictable ground.
translations.idiomatic: I fear flatterers have clouded Your Majesty's judgment, provoking an unjust war and leading us deep into uncertain territory.

sentences.zh: 臣載披典籍，頗識前言，竊見漢武時主父偃、徐樂、嚴安所上書及唐相姚元崇獻明皇十事，忠言至論，可舉而行。

translations.literal: Your servant has repeatedly consulted the classics and knows something of earlier words; I see the memorials submitted in Han Wudi's time by Zhufu Yan, Xu Yue, and Yan An, and the ten matters presented by Tang chancellor Yao Yuanchong to Emperor Ming—loyal words and perfect arguments that could be put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: I have studied the classics and know the precedents: the memorials of Zhufu Yan, Xu Yue, and Yan An in Emperor Wu's Han, and the ten counsels Chancellor Yao Yuanchong offered Emperor Ming of Tang—loyal, penetrating arguments fit to be enacted.

sentences.zh: 伏望萬機之暇，一賜觀覽，其失未遠，雖悔可追。

translations.literal: I humbly hope that in the intervals of your myriad duties Your Majesty will once grant them your reading; the error is not yet far gone, and though you repent it can still be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that amid the myriad affairs of state Your Majesty will read them once; the mistake is not yet beyond repair, and repentance can still avail.

sentences.zh: 臣竊念大發驍雄，動搖百萬之眾，所得者少，所喪者多。

translations.literal: Your servant further reflects that to dispatch brave champions and stir a host of a million yields little gain and costs much loss.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect further that to mobilize elite troops and shake a million men brings little gain at great cost.

sentences.zh: 又聞戰者危事，難保其必勝；

translations.literal: I also hear that war is a perilous affair and victory cannot be assured;
translations.idiomatic: War is perilous, and victory cannot be guaranteed;

sentences.zh: 兵者兇器，深戒於不虞。

translations.literal: arms are an ill-omened instrument, and one must deeply guard against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: arms are instruments of violence, and one must guard deeply against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 所繫甚大，不可不思。

translations.literal: What is at stake is very great; it cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: The stakes are immense; this cannot go unconsidered.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞上古聖人，心無固必，事不凝滯，理貴變通。

translations.literal: Your servant also hears that the sage rulers of high antiquity had minds without fixed obstinacy, affairs without rigid stagnation, and valued reason in adapting to change.
translations.idiomatic: The sage rulers of antiquity held no fixed obstinacy, let no affair stagnate, and prized flexible adaptation.

sentences.zh: 前書有「兵久生變」之言，深為可慮，苟或更圖稽緩，轉失機宜。

translations.literal: Earlier writings say that 'prolonged warfare breeds change'—this is deeply to be feared; if one seeks instead to deliberate further and delay, one will miss the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: The classics warn that prolonged war breeds mutiny—deeply alarming; if we hesitate and delay further, we will miss the moment.

sentences.zh: 旬朔之間，時涉秋序，邊庭早涼，弓勁馬肥，我軍久困，切慮此際，或誤指蹤。

translations.literal: Within ten days and a month the season will touch autumn; on the frontier early cool comes, bows are strong and horses fat, while our army has long been exhausted—I deeply fear that at such a time our movements may be misdirected.
translations.idiomatic: Within weeks autumn will come; on the frontier the air turns cool early, bows are taut and horses strong, while our troops are long exhausted—I fear our commands may go astray at just such a moment.

sentences.zh: 臣方冒寵以守藩，曷敢興言而沮眾。

translations.literal: Your servant now enjoys favor yet guards a frontier post—how dare I raise my voice to dampen the army's spirit?
translations.idiomatic: I now hold favor yet guard a frontier post—how dare I speak out and discourage the troops?

sentences.zh: 蓋臣已日薄西山，餘光無幾，酬恩報國，正在斯時。

translations.literal: Yet your servant's sun already sets over the western hills, and little light remains; to repay grace and serve the state—the time is now.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my sun already sets over the western hills and little light remains; to repay grace and serve the state—the moment is now.

sentences.zh: 伏望速詔班師，無容玩敵。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will quickly decree withdrawal and not treat the enemy lightly.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to order withdrawal at once and not underestimate the foe.

sentences.zh: 臣復有全策，願達聖聰。

translations.literal: Your servant has further a complete strategy and wishes it to reach Your Majesty's clear hearing.
translations.idiomatic: I have further a full strategy and wish it to reach Your Majesty's ear.

sentences.zh: 望陛下精調御膳，保養聖躬，挈彼疲氓，轉之富庶。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will carefully regulate the imperial diet, preserve your sacred person, lift up those weary people, and turn them toward wealth and plenty.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will tend your health, care for your sacred person, lift the weary people, and turn them toward prosperity.

sentences.zh: 將見邊烽不警，外戶不扃，率土歸仁，殊方異俗，相率嚮化，契丹獨將焉往？

translations.literal: Then you will see frontier beacons unlit, outer doors unbarred, all within the realm turning to benevolence, and peoples of strange lands and customs coming one after another to accept transformation—whither alone can the Khitan go?
translations.idiomatic: Then frontier alarms will fall silent, outer gates need no bolt, the realm will turn to benevolent rule, and distant peoples will one after another accept civilization—where then can the Khitan alone flee?

sentences.zh: 陛下計不出此，乃信邪謅之徒，謂契丹主少事多，所以用武，以中陛下之意。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty's plan does not go by this, then you believe the deceivers who say the Khitan ruler is young and affairs are many, and therefore use force to hit upon Your Majesty's intent.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty's plan is not this, then you trust deceivers who say the Khitan ruler is young and burdened with affairs, and therefore resort to war to gratify Your Majesty's wishes.

sentences.zh: 陛下樂禍求功，以為萬全，臣竊以為不可。

translations.literal: Your Majesty delights in calamity and seeks merit, thinking it perfectly safe; your servant privately thinks this cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty takes pleasure in inviting disaster while seeking glory, believing all is secure—I cannot agree.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下審其虛實，究其妄謬，正奸臣誤國之罪，罷將士伐燕之師。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will examine truth and falsehood, investigate delusion and error, correct the crime of treacherous ministers who misled the state, and withdraw the troops and officers campaigning against Yan.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to sift truth from falsehood, expose delusion and error, punish the treacherous ministers who misled the state, and withdraw the army campaigning against Yan.

sentences.zh: 非特多難興王，抑亦從諫則聖也。

translations.literal: It is not only that many tribulations raise up kings; moreover, he who accepts remonstrance becomes sage.
translations.idiomatic: Not only do tribulations test and temper a ruler—he who heeds remonstrance proves himself sage.

sentences.zh: 古之人尚聞屍諫，老臣未死，豈敢百諛為安身之計而不言哉？」

translations.literal: Men of antiquity even heard of remonstrance unto death; this old minister not yet dead—how dare I devise a hundred flatteries as a plan for self-preservation and not speak?
translations.idiomatic: Men of old would remonstrate even unto death; though I am old, I am not yet dead—how could I resort to flattery to save myself and keep silent?

sentences.zh: 帝賜手詔曰：

translations.literal: The Emperor bestowed a handwritten edict, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent a personal edict in reply:

sentences.zh: 「朕昨者興師選將，止令曹彬、米信等頓於雄、霸，裹糧坐甲以張軍聲。

translations.literal: I recently raised an army and chose generals, only ordering Cao Bin, Mi Xin, and others to encamp at Xiong and Ba, wrapping provisions and sitting in armor to display military might.
translations.idiomatic: When I recently raised troops and chose commanders, I had Cao Bin, Mi Xin, and others encamp at Xiongzhou and Bazhou with rations packed and armor donned, simply to display our military presence.

sentences.zh: 俟一兩月間山後平定，潘美、田重進等會兵以進，直抵幽州，然後控扼險固，恢復舊疆，此朕之志也。

translations.literal: After one or two months, when the lands beyond the mountains were pacified, Pan Mei, Tian Chongjin, and others would join forces and advance straight to Youzhou, then seize the strategic passes and recover the old borders—this was my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Once the region beyond the mountains was pacified in a month or two, Pan Mei, Tian Chongjin, and others were to unite their forces, march straight to Youzhou, seize the strategic passes, and recover our lost territory—that was my plan.

sentences.zh: 奈何將帥等不遵成算，各騁所見，領十萬甲士出塞遠鬥，速取其郡縣，更還師以援輜重，往復勞弊，為遼人所襲，此責在主將也。

translations.literal: Alas, the generals did not follow the settled plan, each pursuing his own views, leading a hundred thousand armored soldiers beyond the frontier for distant combat, quickly seizing their commanderies and counties, then returning to support the baggage train—to and fro in exhaustion, ambushed by the Liao people—this blame lies with the chief commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the commanders ignored the settled plan, each following his own judgment, leading a hundred thousand armored troops beyond the frontier in reckless advance, seizing towns and counties in haste, then doubling back to protect the supply train—exhausted by the to-and-fro, they were ambushed by the Liao. The blame rests with the chief commanders.

sentences.zh: 況朕踵百王之末，粗致承平，蓋念彼民陷於邊患，將救焚而拯溺，匪黷武以佳兵，卿當悉之也。

translations.literal: Moreover I follow upon the end of a hundred kings, having roughly achieved peace, thinking only that those people are trapped in frontier calamity—I mean to rescue from fire and save from drowning, not to abuse warfare with fine troops—you should understand this fully.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I reign at the end of an age of kings and have roughly restored peace. I act only because those people suffer on the frontier—I mean to rescue the burning and save the drowning, not to indulge in belligerence. You should understand this.

sentences.zh: 疆場之事，已為之備，卿勿為憂。

translations.literal: Frontier affairs have already been provided for; you need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier is already guarded; you need not worry.

sentences.zh: 卿社稷元臣，忠言苦口，三復來奏，嘉愧實深。」

translations.literal: You are a founding minister of the altars of soil and grain; your loyal words are bitter medicine; thrice you have submitted memorials—I am deeply moved and shamed.
translations.idiomatic: You are a pillar of the state. Your loyal counsel, however bitter, has reached me three times. I am deeply moved—and deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 普表謝曰：

translations.literal: Pu submitted a memorial of thanks, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu submitted a memorial of thanks:

sentences.zh: 「昨以天兵久駐塞外，未克恢復，漸及炎蒸，事危勢迫，輙陳狂狷，甘俟憲章。

translations.literal: Yesterday, because the imperial army long encamped beyond the frontier and could not recover the territory, gradually reaching torrid heat, the affair dangerous and the situation urgent, I rashly presented wild obstinacy, willingly awaiting punishment under the law.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, seeing the imperial army long encamped beyond the frontier without recovering our territory, as the torrid season drew near and the crisis pressed, I rashly spoke my stubborn mind, prepared to accept whatever punishment the law might impose.

sentences.zh: 陛下特鑒衷誠，親紆宸翰，密諭聖謀。

translations.literal: Your Majesty especially discerned my inner sincerity, personally extended your imperial brush, and secretly instructed me of your sacred strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty saw my sincere intent, personally wrote in your own hand, and confided your sacred strategy to me.

sentences.zh: 臣竊審命師討罪，信為上策，將帥能遵成算，必可平定。

translations.literal: Your servant privately judges that dispatching troops to punish crime is truly the superior strategy; if generals can follow the settled plan, pacification is certain.
translations.idiomatic: I now see that dispatching troops to punish the enemy was indeed the right strategy. Had the commanders followed the settled plan, success was assured.

sentences.zh: 惟其不副天心，由茲敗事。

translations.literal: Only they did not accord with Heaven's intent, and thus the affair failed.
translations.idiomatic: Only because they did not accord with Heaven's intent did the campaign fail.

sentences.zh: 今既邊鄙有備，更復何虞。

translations.literal: Now that the frontier is already prepared, what further worry?
translations.idiomatic: Now that the frontier is guarded, what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 況陛下登極十年，坐隆大業，無一物之失所，見萬國之咸寧。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty has ascended the throne ten years, sitting in the rise of a great enterprise—not one thing lost from its place, seeing all states equally at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty has reigned ten years and presided over a flourishing empire—nothing lost from its place, all lands at peace.

sentences.zh: 所宜端拱穆清，嗇神和志，自可遠繼九皇，俯觀五帝。

translations.literal: What is fitting is to sit upright with hands folded in reverent purity, husband spirit and harmonize intent—then naturally one can far inherit the Nine Emperors and look down upon the Five Thearchs.
translations.idiomatic: You need only govern with quiet dignity, conserve your spirit and inner composure, and you may emulate the ancient Nine Emperors and the Five Thearchs below them.

sentences.zh: 豈必窮邊極武，與契丹較勝負哉？

translations.literal: Must one necessarily exhaust the frontier and push warfare to its limit, comparing victory and defeat with the Khitan?
translations.idiomatic: Must you exhaust yourself on the frontier and measure strength against the Khitan?

sentences.zh: 臣素虧壯志，矧在衰齡，雖無功伐，願竭忠純。」

translations.literal: Your servant has long lacked robust ambition, moreover in declining years; though without merit in campaigning, I wish to exhaust my loyal purity.
translations.idiomatic: I have long lacked strength of purpose, and now in my declining years I can offer no military service—yet I wish to devote what loyalty remains.

sentences.zh: 觀者咸嘉其忠。

translations.literal: Observers all praised his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Those who witnessed it all praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 四年，移山南東道節度，自梁國公改封許國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to military governor of Shannan East Circuit, his title changed from Duke of Liang to Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he was made military governor of Shannan East Circuit, his title changing from Duke of Liang to Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 會詔下親耕籍田，普表求入覲，辭甚懇切。

translations.literal: When an edict was issued for the emperor's personal plowing of the sacred field, Pu submitted a memorial requesting an audience; his words were very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict summoned the emperor to plow the sacred field, Pu submitted a memorial begging to attend court; his words were deeply earnest.

sentences.zh: 上惻然謂宰相曰：「普開國元臣，朕所尊禮，宜從其請。」

translations.literal: The Emperor, moved, said to the chief ministers: Pu is a founding minister of the dynasty, whom I honor and respect—his request should be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, the Emperor said to the chief ministers: "Pu is a founding minister of the dynasty, whom I honor and esteem. His request should be granted.

sentences.zh: 既至，慰撫數四，普嗚咽流涕。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the Emperor comforted him repeatedly; Pu sobbed with streaming tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu arrived, the Emperor comforted him again and again; Pu sobbed with streaming tears.

sentences.zh: 陳王元僖上言曰：

translations.literal: Prince of Chen Yuanxi submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuanxi of Chen submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 「臣伏見唐太宗有魏玄成、房玄齡、杜如晦，明皇有姚崇、宋璟、魏知古，皆任以輔弼，委之心膂，財成帝道，康濟九區，宗祀延洪，史策昭煥，良由登用得其人也。

translations.literal: Your servant has seen that Tang Taizong had Wei Zheng, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui; Ming Huang had Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Wei Zhigu—all entrusted as assistants, confided to as heart and backbone, completing the imperial Way, bringing ease to the nine regions, extending ancestral sacrifice in abundance, histories shining bright—truly because in appointing them he obtained the right men.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Emperor Taizong of Tang had Wei Zheng, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui; Emperor Xuanzong had Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Wei Zhigu. Each entrusted his ministers as true counselors, relying on them as his very heart and sinew. They perfected the imperial Way, brought peace to the realm, ensured enduring ancestral rites, and left histories that shine—all because the right men were appointed.

sentences.zh: 今陛下君臨萬方，焦勞庶政，宵衣旰食，以民為心。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty rules the myriad regions, toiling over all affairs, rising before dawn and eating after dusk, taking the people as your heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now rules all under Heaven, laboring over every affair, rising before dawn and dining after dusk, with the people's welfare always at heart.

sentences.zh: 歷考前王，誠無所讓，而輔相之重，未偕曩賢。

translations.literal: Examining former kings, truly there is nothing to yield; yet the weight of the chief minister does not match those former worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the kings of old, Your Majesty yields to none—yet the weight borne by your chief ministers falls short of those former worthies.

sentences.zh: 況為邦在於任人，任人在乎公正，公正之道莫先於賞罰，斯為政之大柄也。

translations.literal: Moreover governing a state lies in appointing men; appointing men lies in fairness; in the way of fairness nothing comes before rewards and punishments—this is the great handle of government.
translations.idiomatic: Governing a state depends on appointing the right men; appointing men depends on fairness—and fairness begins with rewards and punishments. This is the sovereign lever of rule.

sentences.zh: 茍賞罰匪當，淑慝莫分，朝廷紀綱，漸致隳紊。

translations.literal: If rewards and punishments are not proper, good and evil cannot be distinguished, and the court's laws and discipline gradually fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards and punishments miscarry, good and evil blur, and the court's discipline gradually unravels.

sentences.zh: 必須公正之人典衡軸，直躬敢言，以辨得失，然後彝倫式序，庶務用康。

translations.literal: One must have fair men hold the pivot of power, stand upright and dare to speak, to distinguish gain and loss—then the moral order is set in array and all affairs find ease.
translations.idiomatic: Fair-minded men must hold the levers of power, stand upright, and speak boldly to distinguish right from wrong—only then will moral order prevail and all affairs prosper.

sentences.zh: 伏見山南東道節度使趙普，開國元老，參謀締構，厚重有識，不妄希求恩顧以全祿位，不私徇人情以邀名望，此真聖朝之良臣也。

translations.literal: I humbly see Zhao Pu, military governor of Shannan East Circuit—founding elder, counselor in founding and construction, stolid and perceptive, not rashly seeking favor to preserve salary and rank, not privately indulging personal ties to chase reputation—truly a good minister of this sage court.
translations.idiomatic: I see Zhao Pu, military governor of Shannan East Circuit—a founding elder who helped shape the dynasty, stolid and wise. He does not seek favor to preserve his salary, nor indulge private ties to chase reputation. He is a true minister of this court.

sentences.zh: 竊聞憸巧之輩，朋黨比周，眾口嗷嗷，惡直醜正，恨不斥逐遐徼，以快其心。

translations.literal: I secretly hear that crafty and artful sorts form factions and band together, mouths clamoring together, hating the upright and uglifying the correct, hating that they are not driven off to distant frontiers to satisfy their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that the crafty and cunning band together in factions, their voices raised in clamor, hating the upright and reviling the honest—they long to banish such men to distant frontiers to satisfy themselves.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 蓋慮陛下之再用普也。

translations.literal: Because they fear Your Majesty will employ Pu again.
translations.idiomatic: Because they fear Your Majesty will restore Pu to power.

sentences.zh: 然公讜之人，咸願陛下復委以政，啟沃君心，羽翼聖化。

translations.literal: Yet men of public reputation all wish Your Majesty would again entrust him with government, to nourish your heart and wing the sage transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet honorable men everywhere wish Your Majesty would restore him to office—to nourish your judgment and strengthen your sage rule.

sentences.zh: 國有大事，使之謀之；

translations.literal: When the state has great affairs, let him plan them;
translations.idiomatic: When the state faces great affairs, let him plan them;

sentences.zh: 朝有宏綱，使之舉之；

translations.literal: when the court has great principles, let him uphold them;
translations.idiomatic: when the court has great principles, let him uphold them;

sentences.zh: 四目未察，使之明之；

translations.literal: where the four eyes have not seen, let him make clear;
translations.idiomatic: where your four eyes have not seen, let him make clear;

sentences.zh: 四聰未至，使之達之。

translations.literal: where the four ears have not reached, let him convey it.
translations.idiomatic: where your four ears have not reached, let him convey it.

sentences.zh: 官人以材，則無竊祿，致君以道，則無苟容。

translations.literal: Appoint men by talent, then none steal salary; lead the ruler by the Way, then none indulge recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint men by talent and none will hold office undeserved; guide the ruler by the Way and none will gain favor unworthily.

sentences.zh: 賢愚洞分，玉石殊致，當使結朋黨以馳驁聲勢者氣索，縱巧佞以援引儕類者道消。

translations.literal: The worthy and foolish clearly divided, jade and stone differently displayed—then those who form factions to parade their power should lose breath, those who indulge craft and flattery to pull in their kind should see their path vanish.
translations.idiomatic: When worthy and unworthy are clearly told apart, jade from common stone, those who parade in factions will lose their swagger, and the crafty flatterers who pull in their own kind will find their path blocked.

sentences.zh: 沈冥廢滯得以進，名儒懿行得以顯，大政何患乎不舉，生民何患乎不康，匪窬期月之間，可臻清靜之治。

translations.literal: The obscure and stalled may advance, famous scholars and fine conduct may shine forth—what worry that great governance is not uplifted, what worry that the people are not at ease? Within not a full month, one may reach quiet and clean rule.
translations.idiomatic: The obscure and overlooked may rise, eminent scholars and exemplary conduct may shine forth—then why fear that great affairs will not succeed, or that the people will not prosper? Within a month, tranquil order may be achieved.

sentences.zh: 臣知慮庸淺，發言魯直。

translations.literal: Your servant's knowledge and thought are shallow and mean; my words are blunt and straight.
translations.idiomatic: My understanding is shallow and my words blunt.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下旁采群議，俯察物情，苟用不失，實邦國大幸。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will gather opinions from all sides, look down and observe the people's sentiment—if employment is not mistaken, truly it is the state's great fortune.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to heed counsel from every quarter and discern the people's wishes. If you appoint him, the state will be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 耤田禮畢，太宗欲相呂蒙正，以其新進，藉普舊德為之表率，冊拜太保兼侍中。

translations.literal: When the sacred-field rites were complete, Taizong wished to make Lü Mengzheng chief minister; because he was newly advanced, he relied on Pu's old virtue as a model, and invested him as Grand Preceptor concurrently Palace Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: When the plowing rites concluded, Taizong wished to appoint Lü Mengzheng chief minister. Because Lü was newly risen, he drew on Pu's established stature as a model and invested Pu as Grand Preceptor and concurrently Palace Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 帝謂之曰：「卿國之勳舊，朕所毗倚，古人恥其君不及堯、舜，卿其念哉。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to him: You are an old meritorious servant of the state, whom I rely upon—the ancients were shamed if their lord did not reach Yao and Shun; keep this in mind.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to him: "You are an old servant of merit on whom I rely. The ancients were shamed if their ruler fell short of Yao and Shun—bear this in mind.

sentences.zh: 普頓首謝。

translations.literal: Pu prostrated himself and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 時樞密副使趙昌言與胡旦、陳象輿、董儼、梁顥厚善。

translations.literal: At the time Deputy Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhao Changyan was on close terms with Hu Dan, Chen Xiangyu, Dong Yan, and Liang Hao.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Deputy Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhao Changyan was on close terms with Hu Dan, Chen Xiangyu, Dong Yan, and Liang Hao.

sentences.zh: 會旦令翟馬周上封事，排毀時政，普深嫉之，奏流馬周，黜昌言等。

translations.literal: When Dan had Zhai Mazhou submit a sealed memorial attacking current policy, Pu deeply resented this, memorialized to exile Mazhou, and demoted Changyan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Dan had Zhai Mazhou submit a sealed memorial denouncing current policy, Pu deeply resented it. He memorialized to exile Mazhou and demote Changyan and the others.

sentences.zh: 鄭州團練使侯莫陳利用驕肆僭侈，大為不法，普廉得之，盡以條奏，利用坐流商州，普固請誅之。

translations.literal: Zhengzhou regimental trainer Hou Mochen Liyong was arrogant, extravagant, and usurpatory, greatly breaking the law. Pu learned of it through investigation and submitted detailed memorials; Liyong was exiled to Shangzhou for his crime, and Pu firmly requested his execution.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Mochen Liyong, regimental trainer of Zhengzhou, was arrogant, extravagant, and lawless. Pu investigated and reported every detail; Liyong was exiled to Shangzhou for his crimes, and Pu pressed for his execution.

sentences.zh: 其嫉惡強直皆此類。

translations.literal: His hatred of the strong and straight was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His hatred of the forceful and upright took this form throughout.

sentences.zh: 李繼遷之擾邊，普建議以趙保忠復領夏臺故地，因令圖之。

translations.literal: When Li Jiqian troubled the frontier, Pu proposed that Zhao Baozhong be restored to his old lands in Xiatang, and ordered a plot accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiqian troubled the frontier, Pu proposed restoring Zhao Baozhong to his old Xia lands and ordered a plot to that end.

sentences.zh: 保忠反與繼遷同謀為邊患，時論歸咎於普，頗為同列所窺，不得專決。

translations.literal: Baozhong instead joined with Jiqian in plotting frontier trouble; contemporary opinion blamed Pu, and he was somewhat watched by his colleagues, unable to decide alone.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhong instead conspired with Jiqian to trouble the frontier. Public opinion blamed Pu, and his colleagues looked on him with suspicion; he could no longer decide affairs alone.

sentences.zh: 舊制，宰相以未時歸第，是歲大熱，特許普夏中至午時歸私第。

translations.literal: By old rule, chief ministers returned home at the wei hour; that year was very hot, and Pu was specially permitted to return to his private residence by noon in midsummer.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, chief ministers returned home at the wei hour; that year was fiercely hot, and Pu was specially permitted to leave for home by noon in midsummer.

sentences.zh: 明年，免朝謁，止日赴中書視事，有大政則召對。

translations.literal: The next year he was exempted from court audience, going only daily to the Secretariat to handle affairs; for great policies he was summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was exempted from court audiences, attending the Secretariat daily to transact business; for major affairs he was summoned for private audience.

sentences.zh: 冬，被疾請告，車駕屢幸其第省之，賜予加等。

translations.literal: In winter he fell ill and requested leave; the imperial carriage repeatedly visited his residence to inquire; gifts were increased in grade.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he fell ill and requested leave. The Emperor repeatedly visited his home to inquire after him, granting gifts of extra rank.

sentences.zh: 普遂稱疾篤，三上表求致仕，上勉從之，以普為西京留守、河南尹，依前守太保兼中書令。

translations.literal: Pu then declared his illness grave, thrice submitted memorials requesting retirement; the Emperor reluctantly consented, appointing Pu Western Capital Administrator and Henan Intendant, continuing as before Grand Preceptor concurrently Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Pu declared his illness grave and thrice memorialized to retire. The Emperor reluctantly agreed, appointing him Administrator of the Western Capital and Intendant of Henan while retaining his titles of Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 普三表懇讓。

translations.literal: Pu thrice submitted memorials earnestly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Pu thrice memorialized earnestly to decline.

sentences.zh: 賜手詔曰：「開國舊勳，惟卿一人，不同他等，無至固讓，俟首塗有日，當就第與卿為別。」

translations.literal: An handwritten edict was bestowed: Of the founding old merit, you alone are different from the rest—do not persist in declining. When the day of your final journey comes, I shall come to your residence to take leave of you.
translations.idiomatic: A personal edict was sent: "Among the founding ministers, you alone stand apart. Do not persist in declining. When the day of your final journey comes, I shall visit your home to bid you farewell.

sentences.zh: 普捧詔涕泣，因力疾請對，賜坐移晷，頗言及國家事，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: Pu received the edict with streaming tears, then despite his illness forcefully requested audience; he was granted a seat until the sundial moved, spoke considerably of state affairs, and the Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Pu received the edict with streaming tears and, despite his illness, requested audience. Granted a seat until the sundial moved, he spoke at length of state affairs, and the Emperor praised and accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 普將發，車駕幸其第。

translations.literal: As Pu was about to depart, the imperial carriage visited his residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu was about to depart, the Emperor visited his home.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年春，以老衰久病，令留守通判劉昌言奉表求致政，中使馳傳撫問，凡三上表乞骸骨。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year of Chunhua, owing to old age, decline, and long illness, he had acting administrator and vice-prefect Liu Changyan submit a memorial requesting retirement; imperial emissaries raced by relay to inquire after him; in all he thrice submitted memorials begging leave of his bones.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the third year of Chunhua, aged and long ill, he had Liu Changyan, acting administrator and vice-prefect, submit a memorial requesting retirement. Imperial emissaries raced by relay to inquire after him. In all he thrice begged to retire.

sentences.zh: 拜太師，封魏國公，給宰相奉料，令養疾，俟損日赴闕，仍遣其弟宗正少卿安易齎詔書賜之。

translations.literal: He was invested Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed Duke of Wei, granted chief minister's salary, ordered to nurse his illness, to come to court when recovered, and his younger brother Vice-Director of the Court of Imperial Clan Anyi was still dispatched to bear the edict and bestow it.
translations.idiomatic: He was invested Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed Duke of Wei, granted a chief minister's salary, and ordered to nurse his illness and come to court when recovered. His younger brother Anyi, Vice-Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, was dispatched to deliver the edict.

sentences.zh: 又特遣使賜普詔曰：「卿頃屬微疴，懇求致政，朕以居守之重，慮煩耆耋，維師之命，用表尊賢。

translations.literal: Again a special emissary was dispatched to bestow on Pu an edict: You recently suffered a slight ailment and earnestly sought retirement; I, owing to the weight of guarding the capital, feared to trouble the aged, and the appointment of Grand Preceptor was to show esteem for the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: A special emissary was again dispatched with an edict for Pu: "You recently fell ill and earnestly sought to retire. Given the weight of my duties, I feared to burden you in your old age. The title of Grand Preceptor was meant to honor your worth.

sentences.zh: 佇聞有瘳，與朕相見。

translations.literal: I await word of your recovery to meet with me.
translations.idiomatic: I look forward to your recovery and our meeting again.

sentences.zh: 今賜羊酒如別錄，卿宜愛精神，近醫藥，強飲食，以副朕眷遇之意。」

translations.literal: Now I bestow sheep and wine as in the separate record—you should cherish your spirit, seek medicine near at hand, strengthen your food and drink, to accord with my intent of gracious favor.
translations.idiomatic: Now I send sheep and wine as listed separately. Cherish your spirit, keep close to your physicians, eat well—to honor my regard for you.

sentences.zh: 七月，卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he died, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he died, at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 卒之先一歲，普生日，上遣其子承宗齎器幣、鞍馬就賜之，承宗復命未幾卒。

translations.literal: One year before his death, on Pu's birthday, the Emperor sent his son Chengzong bearing ritual vessels, silks, and saddle horses to bestow them; Chengzong returned to report and not long after died.
translations.idiomatic: One year before his death, on Pu's birthday the Emperor sent his son Chengzong with ritual gifts, silks, and saddle horses. Chengzong returned to report—and soon after died.

sentences.zh: 次歲，普已罷中書令，故事，無生辰之賜，特遣普侄婿左正言、直昭文館張秉賜之禮物。

translations.literal: The next year Pu had already relinquished Director of the Secretariat; by precedent there was no birthday gift—yet specially Pu's nephew-in-law Left Remonstrator and Academician of the Zhaowen Hall Zhang Bing was dispatched to bestow gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Pu had already left the office of Director of the Secretariat; by precedent no birthday gifts were given—but the Emperor specially dispatched Zhang Bing, Pu's nephew-in-law, Left Remonstrator and Academician of the Zhaowen Hall, with birthday gifts.

sentences.zh: 普聞之，因追悼承宗，秉未至而普疾篤。

translations.literal: When Pu heard of it, he thus mourned Chengzong; before Bing arrived Pu's illness was grave.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, Pu mourned Chengzong again; before Zhang Bing arrived, Pu's illness had turned grave.

sentences.zh: 先是，普遣親吏甄潛詣上清太平宮致禱，神為降語曰：「趙普，宋朝忠臣，久被病，亦有冤累耳。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Pu sent his personal clerk Zhen Qian to the Shangqing Taiping Palace to offer prayers; the spirit descended with words: Zhao Pu, loyal minister of the Song dynasty, long afflicted with illness—there are also accumulated wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Pu had sent his personal clerk Zhen Qian to the Shangqing Taiping Palace to pray. The spirit spoke: "Zhao Pu, loyal minister of the Song, long stricken with illness—and burdened by wrongs as well.

sentences.zh: 潛還，普力疾冠帶，出中庭受神言，涕泗感咽，是夕卒。

translations.literal: Qian returned; Pu, forcing himself despite illness, donned cap and belt, went out to the central courtyard to receive the spirit's words, weeping with choked emotion; that evening he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian returned, Pu, forcing himself despite his illness, dressed in full regalia and went to the central courtyard to receive the spirit's message, weeping with choked emotion. That evening he died.

sentences.zh: 上聞之震悼。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he was shaken with grief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was deeply shaken by the news.

sentences.zh: 謂近臣曰：「普事先帝，與朕故舊，能斷大事，嚮與朕嘗有不足，眾所知也。

translations.literal: He said to close ministers: Pu served the previous emperor, was an old acquaintance of mine, could decide great affairs; formerly he and I had our shortcomings—all know this.
translations.idiomatic: He told his close ministers: "Pu served the Previous Emperor and was my old friend. He could decide great affairs. It is well known that he and I had our differences in the past.

sentences.zh: 朕君臨以來，每優禮之，普亦傾竭自效，盡忠國家，真社稷臣也，朕甚惜之。」

translations.literal: Since I have ruled, I have always treated him with special honor; Pu also poured himself out in service, giving full loyalty to the state—a true minister of the altars of soil and grain—I deeply mourn his loss.
translations.idiomatic: Since my accession I have always honored him, and he has served with every ounce of devotion—a true pillar of the state. I deeply mourn his loss.

sentences.zh: 因出涕，左右感動。

translations.literal: He wept aloud; those around him were moved.
translations.idiomatic: He wept aloud, and all present were moved.

sentences.zh: 廢朝五日，為出次發哀。

translations.literal: Court was suspended five days; he went out to the mourning pavilion to express grief.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for five days, and the Emperor went out to the mourning pavilion to express his grief.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書令，追封真定王，賜諡忠獻，上撰神道碑銘，親八分書以賜之。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs, posthumously enfeoffed King of Zhending, granted posthumous name Zhongxian; the Emperor composed a spirit-way stele inscription and personally wrote it in eight-part script to bestow.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs, posthumously enfeoffed King of Zhending, and granted the posthumous name Loyal and Distinguished. The Emperor composed an inscription for his spirit-way stele and personally wrote it in clerical script as a gift.

sentences.zh: 遣右諫議大夫范杲攝鴻臚卿，護喪事。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrating Censor Fan Gao was dispatched acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial to oversee funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dispatched Fan Gao, Right Remonstrating Censor, acting as Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 賻絹、布各五百匹，米、麫各五百石。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts of silk and cloth five hundred bolts each, rice and flour five hundred piculs each.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral gifts were granted: five hundred bolts each of silk and cloth, and five hundred piculs each of rice and flour.

sentences.zh: 葬日，有司設鹵簿鼓吹如式。

translations.literal: On the burial day, the relevant offices set out imperial escort and musical accompaniment according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial, the proper offices arranged the imperial escort and ceremonial music according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 二女皆笄，普妻和氏言願為尼，太宗再三諭之，不能奪。

translations.literal: Both daughters had reached adulthood; Pu's wife Lady He said she wished to become a nun; Taizong repeatedly admonished her but could not dissuade her.
translations.idiomatic: Both daughters had come of age. Pu's wife, Lady He, declared she wished to become a nun. Taizong repeatedly urged her to reconsider but could not dissuade her.

sentences.zh: 賜長女名志願，號智果大師；

translations.literal: The elder daughter was granted the name Zhiyuan, titled Great Master Zhiguo;
translations.idiomatic: The elder daughter was given the name Zhiyuan and the title Great Master Zhiguo;

sentences.zh: 次女名志英，號智圓大師。

translations.literal: The younger daughter was named Zhiying, titled Great Master Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The younger was named Zhiying and titled Great Master Zhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖側微，普從之遊，既有天下，普屢以微時所不足者言之。

translations.literal: At first, when Taizu was of humble station, Pu accompanied him in his wanderings; once he had the realm under Heaven, Pu repeatedly spoke of what was lacking in their early days.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning, when Taizu was still obscure, Pu kept company with him. Once Taizu had the realm, Pu repeatedly spoke of slights from their early days.

sentences.zh: 太祖豁達，謂普曰：「若塵埃中可識天子、宰相，則人皆物色之矣。」

translations.literal: Taizu was magnanimous and said to Pu: If one could recognize Son of Heaven and chief minister in the dust, then everyone would seek them out.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was magnanimous. He said to Pu: "If one could pick out the Son of Heaven and chief minister from the dust, everyone would be searching for them.

sentences.zh: 自是不復言。

translations.literal: From then on he spoke no more of it.
translations.idiomatic: After that Pu never spoke of it again.

sentences.zh: 普少習吏事，寡學術，及為相，太祖常勸以讀書。

translations.literal: Pu in youth practiced clerkly affairs, had little learning; once he became chief minister, Taizu often urged him to read books.
translations.idiomatic: Pu had trained in clerkly work from youth and had little scholarly learning. Once he became chief minister, Taizu often urged him to read.

sentences.zh: 晚年手不釋卷，每歸私第，闔戶啟篋取書，讀之竟日。

translations.literal: In his later years his hand never released a scroll; each time he returned to his private residence, he closed the door, opened a chest and took out books, reading all day.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he never put down his books. Each time he returned home, he shut his door, opened a chest, took out a book, and read all day.

sentences.zh: 及次日臨政，處決如流。

translations.literal: When the next day he presided over government, he decided affairs like flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: The next day at court he disposed of affairs with effortless fluency.

sentences.zh: 既薨，家人發篋視之，則《論語》二十篇也。

translations.literal: After he died, the family opened the chest to look—it was the twenty chapters of the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the family opened the chest—they found only the twenty chapters of the Analects.

sentences.zh: 普性深沈有岸谷，雖多忌克，而能以天下事為己任。

translations.literal: Pu's nature was deep and hidden with steep banks and valleys; though much jealous and grasping, he could take the affairs of all under Heaven as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was deep and reserved, steep as a riverbank—though prone to jealousy, he took the affairs of the realm as his personal charge.

sentences.zh: 宋初，在相位者多齷齪循默，普剛毅果斷，未有其比。

translations.literal: In early Song, many in the chief minister's seat were petty and timidly silent; Pu was firm, resolute, and decisive—none matched him.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Song, most chief ministers were timid and obsequious; Pu alone was firm and decisive—none matched him.

sentences.zh: 嘗奏薦某人為某官，太祖不用，普明日復奏其人，亦不用，明日，普又以其人奏，太祖怒，碎裂奏牘擲地，普顏色不變，跪而拾之以歸，他日補綴舊紙，復奏如初，太祖乃悟，卒用其人。

translations.literal: Once he memorialized recommending a certain man for a certain office; Taizu did not employ him. Pu the next day again memorialized that man—again not employed. The next day Pu again memorialized that man. Taizu grew angry, tore the memorial to pieces and threw it to the ground. Pu's expression did not change; he knelt, picked up the pieces and returned home. Another day he patched the old paper and memorialized again as before. Taizu then understood and finally employed the man.
translations.idiomatic: Once he recommended a certain man for office; Taizu refused. The next day Pu recommended him again—again refused. The next day Pu recommended him once more. Taizu flew into a rage, tore the memorial to shreds, and threw it to the floor. Pu's expression never changed. He knelt, gathered the pieces, and went home. Later he patched the torn paper and submitted the memorial again unchanged. Taizu at last understood and appointed the man.

sentences.zh: 又有群臣當遷官，太祖素惡其人，不與，普堅以為請，太祖怒曰：「朕固不為遷官。

translations.literal: Again there was a case where a minister was due for promotion; Taizu had long disliked the man and would not grant it. Pu firmly pressed the request. Taizu angrily said: I firmly will not grant the promotion.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion a minister was due for promotion; Taizu had long disliked the man and refused. Pu pressed the matter firmly. Taizu angrily said: "I will not grant this promotion.

sentences.zh: 卿若之何？」

translations.literal: What can you do about it?
translations.idiomatic: What can you do about it?

sentences.zh: 普曰：「刑以懲惡，賞以酬功，古今通道也。

translations.literal: Pu said: Punishment is to chastise evil, reward is to repay merit—this is the universal Way from antiquity to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Pu said: "Punishment chastises evil and reward repays merit—that is the universal Way from antiquity to the present.

sentences.zh: 且刑賞天下之刑賞，非陛下之刑賞，豈得以喜怒專之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, punishment and reward are the punishment and reward of all under Heaven, not Your Majesty's punishment and reward—how can they be wielded solely according to pleasure and anger?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, punishments and rewards belong to the realm, not to Your Majesty alone—how can you wield them purely at the whim of your moods?

sentences.zh: 太祖怒甚，起，普亦隨之。

translations.literal: The Emperor Taizu was exceedingly angry and rose; Pu also followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu flew into a rage and stood up; Pu followed right after him.

sentences.zh: 太祖入宮，普立于宮門，久之不去，竟得俞允。

translations.literal: Taizu entered the palace; Pu stood at the palace gate and for a long time did not leave, and in the end obtained approval.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu went into the palace. Pu stood at the gate and refused to leave. In the end he won his point.

sentences.zh: 太宗入弭德超之讒，疑曹彬不軌，屬普再相，為彬辨雪保證，事狀明白。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne he quelled De Chao's slander, suspected Cao Bin of improper conduct, and entrusted Pu again as chief minister; Pu cleared and vouched for Bin—the facts were clear.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne he put an end to De Chao's slander and came to suspect Cao Bin of disloyalty. With Pu again as chief minister, Pu spoke in Bin's defense and cleared his name—the facts spoke for themselves.

sentences.zh: 太宗歎曰：「朕聽斷不明，幾誤國事。」

translations.literal: Taizong sighed and said: "My judgments are unclear—I nearly erred in state affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sighed: "My judgment was clouded—I nearly let state affairs go wrong."

sentences.zh: 即日竄逐德超，遇彬如舊。

translations.literal: That same day he banished De Chao and treated Bin as before.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he banished De Chao and treated Bin exactly as before.

sentences.zh: 祖吉守郡為姦利，事覺下獄，案劾爰書未具，郊禮將近，太宗疾其貪墨，遣中使諭旨執政曰：「郊赦可特勿貸祖吉。」

translations.literal: Zu Ji, while governing a prefecture, engaged in illicit profit; when the matter was discovered he was imprisoned. The investigation and indictment documents were not yet complete. The suburban sacrifice was approaching. Taizong abhorred his corruption and sent a palace envoy to instruct the chief ministers: "At the suburban amnesty, Zu Ji may specially be denied pardon."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ji had profited corruptly while governing a prefecture. When the scheme was uncovered he was thrown in prison, though the case and indictment were not yet complete. With the suburban sacrifice approaching, Taizong, disgusted by his graft, sent a palace envoy to tell the chief ministers: "At the suburban amnesty, make a special exception—do not pardon Zu Ji."

sentences.zh: 普奏曰：「敗官抵罪，宜正刑辟。

translations.literal: Pu memorialized: "Corrupt officials who merit punishment should properly face execution.
translations.idiomatic: Pu memorialized: "An official who betrays his office deserves proper punishment under the law.

sentences.zh: 然國家卜郊肆類，對越天地，告於神明，奈何以吉而隳陛下赦令哉？」

translations.literal: Yet the state is fixing the date for the suburban sacrifice and grand feasts, facing Heaven and Earth and reporting to the spirits—how can we with Zu Ji ruin Your Majesty's amnesty decree?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the state is preparing the suburban sacrifice and grand rites, facing Heaven and Earth and making report to the spirits—how can we let one man's case wreck Your Majesty's amnesty?"

sentences.zh: 太宗善其言，乃止。

translations.literal: Taizong approved his words and thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong agreed and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 真宗咸平初，追封韓王。

translations.literal: In the early Xianping era of Zhenzong, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianping era under Zhenzong, Pu was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔曰：「故太師贈尚書令、追封韓王趙普，識冠人彝，才高王佐，翊戴興運，光啟鴻圖，雖呂望肆伐之勳，蕭何指縱之效，殆無以過也。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict said: "The late Grand Preceptor, posthumously granted Minister of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed as Prince of Han, Zhao Pu—his insight topped all human norms, his talent exceeded that of a royal assistant; he supported and crowned the rising fortune and opened the great plan. Though the merit of Lü Wang in openly campaigning in war and Xiao He's effect in directing strategy—scarcely could one surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year an edict declared: "The late Grand Preceptor Zhao Pu, posthumously granted Minister of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed as Prince of Han, surpassed all others in wisdom and stood among the greatest of royal counselors. He supported the dynasty at its founding and helped open its grand design. The achievements of Lü Wang on campaign and Xiao He in directing strategy scarcely exceed his.

sentences.zh: 自輔弼兩朝，周旋三紀，茂巖廊之碩望，分屏翰之劇權，正直不回，始終無玷，謀猷可復，風烈如生。

translations.literal: From assisting and supporting two reigns, moving through three decades, his abundant stature in the hall of state, sharing the heavy authority of regional bulwarks—upright and unbending, without stain from beginning to end; his stratagems can be reviewed, his spirit as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: He had served two reigns as chief counselor across three decades, filling the halls of state with his stature and bearing the heavy burden of frontier command. Upright and unyielding, he remained unstained from first to last; his counsel can still be read, and his spirit seems alive.

sentences.zh: 宜預享於大烝，永同休于宗祏，茲為茂典，以答舊勳，其以普配饗太祖廟庭。」

translations.literal: It is fitting that he share in the great autumn sacrifice, forever sharing blessings in the ancestral temple—this is an abundant rite to answer old merit; let Pu be paired in sacrifice at Taizu's temple courtyard."
