translations.idiomatic: Let him share in the great autumn sacrifice and forever partake of blessings in the ancestral temple. This abundant rite honors his old service—let Pu be paired in sacrifice in Taizu's temple courtyard."

sentences.zh: 普子承宗，羽林大將軍，知潭、鄆二州，皆有聲；

translations.literal: Pu's son Chengzong was a general of the Palace Feathered Forest and governed the two prefectures of Tan and Yun—both with reputation;
translations.idiomatic: Pu's son Chengzong, a general of the Palace Feathered Forest, governed Tan and Yun prefectures—both with distinction;

sentences.zh: 承煦，成州團練使。

translations.literal: Chengxu was military training commissioner of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxu served as military training commissioner of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 弟固、安易。

translations.literal: Younger brothers Gu and Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers were Gu and Anyi.

sentences.zh: 固至都官郎中。

translations.literal: Gu rose to director in the Bureau of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gu rose to the position of director in the Bureau of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 弟 安易

translations.literal: Younger brother Anyi
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Anyi

sentences.zh: 安易，字季和。

translations.literal: Anyi, style name Jihe.
translations.idiomatic: Anyi, whose style name was Jihe,

sentences.zh: 建隆初，攝府州錄事參軍，節度使折德扆言其清幹，遂命即真。

translations.literal: In the early Jianlong era, he held the acting post of registrar of Fuzhou; Military Commissioner Zhe Deyi spoke of his integrity and competence, and he was ordered to assume the post in regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianlong era he served as acting registrar of Fuzhou. Military Commissioner Zhe Deyi praised his integrity and capability, and he was confirmed in the post.

sentences.zh: 再遷河南府推官。

translations.literal: He was twice transferred to investigating officer of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice promoted, ending as investigating officer of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會普居相位，十年不赴調。

translations.literal: When Pu occupied the chief minister's seat, for ten years he did not go to office reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: While Pu served as chief minister, Anyi went ten years without requesting a new posting.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，歷華、邢二鎮掌書記。

translations.literal: In the Taiping Xingguo era, he successively served as chief secretary at the two garrisons of Hua and Xing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo era he served in turn as chief secretary at the Hua and Xing garrisons.

sentences.zh: 部芻糧至太原城下，拜監察御史，知興元府；

translations.literal: Conveying fodder to below the walls of Taiyuan, he was appointed censor and made prefect of Xingyuan;
translations.idiomatic: After delivering fodder to the foot of Taiyuan's walls, he was appointed censor and made prefect of Xingyuan;

sentences.zh: 轉殿中，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: he was transferred to the palace censorate and granted the red fish bag.
translations.idiomatic: he was transferred to the palace censorate and granted the red fish pouch of rank.

sentences.zh: 先是，兩川民輸稅者以鐵錢易銅錢。

translations.literal: Previously, the people of the Two Shu regions who paid taxes exchanged iron cash for copper cash.
translations.idiomatic: Previously taxpayers in the Two Shu regions had to exchange iron cash for copper cash when paying taxes.

sentences.zh: 安易言其非便，請許納鐵錢，詔從之。

translations.literal: Anyi said this was inconvenient and requested permission to pay in iron cash; an edict followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Anyi argued that this was impractical and asked that iron cash be accepted instead; the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 九年，起拜宗正少卿，知定州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was raised and appointed vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and made prefect of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was raised to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and made prefect of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 會以曹璨知州，徙安易為通判，未幾代歸。

translations.literal: When Cao Shen was made prefect, Anyi was transferred to be vice prefect; before long he was relieved and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shen was appointed prefect, Anyi was transferred to vice prefect; shortly afterward he was relieved and recalled.

sentences.zh: 又表求外任，命知耀州，留不遣，命按視北邊事。

translations.literal: Again he memorialized seeking an outside appointment; he was ordered to govern Yaozhou but was detained and not sent; he was ordered to inspect northern frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He again petitioned for an outside appointment and was assigned to govern Yaozhou, but was kept at court and instead ordered to inspect affairs on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，嘗建議以蜀地用鐵錢，准銅錢數倍，小民市易頗為不便，請如劉備時令西川鑄大錢，以十當百。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era, he once proposed that since Shu used iron cash valued at several times copper cash, common people found market exchange quite inconvenient; he requested that, as in Liu Bei's time, Western Shu cast large coins worth ten for one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era he proposed that because Shu used iron cash at several times the value of copper cash, petty traders found commerce burdensome. He asked that Western Shu, as under Liu Bei, cast large coins valued at ten for one hundred.

sentences.zh: 下都省集議，吏部尚書宋琪等言：「劉備時蓋患錢少，因而改作，今安易之請反患錢多，非經久計也。」

translations.literal: It was sent down to the Imperial Secretariat for collective deliberation. Minister of Personnel Song Qi and others said: "In Liu Bei's time they probably suffered from too little coin and therefore changed the system; now Anyi's request instead suffers from too much coin—it is not a long-term plan."
translations.idiomatic: The proposal went to the Imperial Secretariat for debate. Minister of Personnel Song Qi and others argued: "Under Liu Bei the problem was too little coin—that is why the system was changed. Anyi's proposal would address too much coin. It is no lasting solution."

sentences.zh: 而安易論請不已，仍募工鑄大錢百餘進之，極其精好，俄墜殿階皆碎，蓋熔鑠盡其精液矣。

translations.literal: But Anyi argued and petitioned without cease; he still recruited workers to cast more than a hundred large coins and presented them—they were extremely fine and excellent, but soon when dropped on the palace steps they all shattered, probably because the melting had exhausted all the fine essence.
translations.idiomatic: Anyi would not let the matter drop. He hired workers to cast more than a hundred large coins and presented them—they were exquisitely wrought, but when they were dropped on the palace steps they all shattered at once, the alloy having lost whatever fine metal it held.

sentences.zh: 太宗不之詰，猶嘉其用心，賜以金紫，且遣其典鑄。

translations.literal: Taizong did not reproach him but still praised his earnest intent, bestowed upon him gold and purple, and dispatched him to supervise casting.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong did not reprimand him. He still praised his dedication, granted him gold and purple rank, and put him in charge of the mint.

sentences.zh: 既而大有虧耗，歲中裁得三千餘緡，眾議喧然，遂罷之，事具《食貨志》。

translations.literal: Before long there was great loss; in a year barely more than three thousand strings were obtained; public debate became clamorous, and it was thereupon abolished—the matter is fully recorded in the Treatise on Food and Commodities.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the project bled money. In a full year it yielded barely three thousand strings. Public outcry grew loud and the scheme was abandoned—the affair is recorded in full in the Treatise on Food and Commodities.

sentences.zh: 歷知襄、廬二州，就遷宗正卿，歸朝，復領卿職。

translations.literal: He successively governed the two prefectures of Xiang and Lu; he was then promoted to director of the Court of the Imperial Clan; returning to court, he again held the director's post.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Xiang and Lu in turn, was promoted to director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, and after returning to court resumed that office.

sentences.zh: 時屬籍未備，奏請纂錄，咸平初，乃命梁周翰與安易同修。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial clan registers were incomplete; he memorialized requesting compilation; in the early Xianping era, Liang Zhouhan and Anyi were ordered to compile them together.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clan registers were incomplete. He petitioned for them to be compiled. Early in Xianping, Liang Zhouhan and Anyi were ordered to edit them together.

sentences.zh: 安易略涉書傳，性強狠，好談世務，而疏闊不可用。

translations.literal: Anyi had slight exposure to books and classics; his nature was strong and harsh; he loved to discuss worldly affairs, yet was crude and broad—not employable.
translations.idiomatic: Anyi had only a shallow grasp of the classics. He was fierce and obstinate, loved to hold forth on public affairs, and was too crude and impractical to be of use.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗嘗問農政，安易請復井田之制。

translations.literal: Earlier, Taizong once inquired about agricultural policy; Anyi requested restoration of the well-field system.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Taizong once asked about agricultural policy. Anyi proposed restoring the well-field system.

sentences.zh: 又以其家本燕薊，多訪以邊事。

translations.literal: Also because his family originally came from Yan and Ji, Taizong often consulted him on frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Because his family came from Yan and Ji, Taizong also often consulted him on frontier matters.

sentences.zh: 景德初，禮官詳定明德皇太后靈駕發引，于京師壬地權攢，依禮埋懸重，升祔神主。

translations.literal: In the early Jingde era, ritual officials thoroughly determined the departure of Empress Dowager Mingde's spirit carriage for the funeral procession—that at the temporary encoffinment at the ren position in the capital, according to ritual, the suspended weight would be buried and the spirit tablet would be elevated and enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era ritual officials worked out the funeral procession for Empress Dowager Mingde—that at the temporary encoffinment site at the ren compass point in the capital, the suspended weight would be buried by ritual and her spirit tablet elevated and enshrined in the temple.

sentences.zh: 安易上言：

translations.literal: Anyi submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Anyi submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「《禮》云：『既虞作主』，虞者，已葬設吉祭也。

translations.literal: "The Rites says: 'Once the yu rites are performed, make the main tablet.' Yu means after burial, establishing the auspicious sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: "The Rites states: 'Once the yu rites are performed, make the main tablet.' Yu refers to the auspicious sacrifice held after burial.

sentences.zh: 明未葬則未立虞主及神主。

translations.literal: Clearly, if there has been no burial, then neither the yu tablet nor the spirit tablet is established.
translations.idiomatic: This makes clear that before burial neither the yu tablet nor the spirit tablet should be installed.

sentences.zh: 所以周制但鑿木為懸重，以主神靈。

translations.literal: Therefore in Zhou practice they only carved wood as the suspended weight to host the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Zhou practice used only a carved wooden suspended weight to hold the spirit.

sentences.zh: 王后七月而葬，則埋懸重，掩玄堂，凶仗、轀輬車、龍輴之屬焚于柏城訖，始可立虞主。

translations.literal: When a queen consort is buried after seven months, then they bury the suspended weight, cover the dark chamber, and after the mourning accoutrements, enclosed carriage, dragon hearse and the like are burned at Cypress City, only then may the yu tablet be established.
translations.idiomatic: When a queen consort is buried after seven months, they bury the suspended weight and seal the burial chamber. Only after the mourning gear, enclosed hearse, dragon carriage, and the like are burned at Cypress City may the yu tablet be installed.

sentences.zh: 吉仗還京，備九祭，復埋虞主，然後立神主，升廟室。

translations.literal: When the auspicious procession returns to the capital, the nine sacrifices are prepared, the yu tablet is again buried, and only then is the spirit tablet established and elevated to the temple chamber.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral procession returns to the capital in state, the nine sacrifices are held, the yu tablet is buried again, and only then is the spirit tablet made and installed in the temple.

sentences.zh: 自曠古至皇朝，上奉祖宗陵廟行此禮，何以今日乃違典章，苟且升祔，方權攢妄立神主，未大葬輒埋懸重？

translations.literal: From remote antiquity to our dynasty, in serving the ancestral tombs and temples this rite was performed—why today violate the canonical regulations, perfunctorily elevate and enshrine, rashly establish a spirit tablet at a temporary encoffinment, and bury the suspended weight before the great burial?
translations.idiomatic: From remote antiquity through our dynasty, the imperial ancestors' tombs and temples have followed this rite—why violate the canonical regulations today? Why perfunctorily enshrine the tablet, rashly install a spirit tablet at a temporary encoffinment, and bury the suspended weight before the full burial?

sentences.zh: 且棺柩未歸園陵，則神靈豈入太廟？

translations.literal: Moreover, if the coffin has not returned to the imperial mausoleum, how can the spirit enter the Grand Temple?
translations.idiomatic: If the coffin has not yet reached the imperial mausoleum, how can the spirit enter the Grand Temple?

sentences.zh: 奈柏城未焚凶仗，則凶穢唐突祖宗。

translations.literal: If the mourning accoutrements at Cypress City have not been burned, then the impurity of mourning affronts the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: And if the mourning gear at Cypress City has not yet been burned, its impurity would offend the imperial ancestors.

sentences.zh: 望約孝章近例，但於壬地權攢，未立神主升祔，凶儀一切祗奉。

translations.literal: I hope to follow the recent precedent of Empress Xiaozhang—only temporary encoffinment at the ren position, not establishing and enshrining the spirit tablet, and reverently observing all mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we follow the recent precedent of Empress Xiaozhang—temporary encoffinment at the ren site only, no spirit tablet installed or enshrined, and every mourning rite observed scrupulously.

sentences.zh: 俟丙午年靈駕西去園陵，東回祔廟。

translations.literal: Wait until the bingwu year when the spirit carriage goes west to the mausoleum and returns east to enshrine in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the bingwu year, when the spirit carriage goes west to the mausoleum and returns east for enshrinement in the temple.

sentences.zh: 如此則免於顛倒，不利國家。」

translations.literal: In this way one avoids inversion—otherwise it will harm the state."
translations.idiomatic: Only then will we avoid reversing proper order. Otherwise the realm will suffer harm."

sentences.zh: 乃詔有司再加詳定。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the offices to deliberate again in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the relevant offices to review the matter again.

sentences.zh: 判禮院孫何等上言：

translations.literal: Sun He and others of the Court of Ritual submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Sun He of the Court of Ritual and others submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「按《晉書》羊太后崩，廢一時之祀，天地明堂，去樂不作。

translations.literal: "Examining the Book of Jin—when Empress Dowager Yang died, sacrifices for a time were suspended; at Heaven and Earth and the Bright Hall, music was removed and not performed.
translations.idiomatic: "The Book of Jin records that when Empress Dowager Yang died, sacrifices were suspended for a time; at the altars of Heaven and Earth and the Bright Hall, music was omitted.

sentences.zh: 又按《禮》，王后崩，五祀之祭不行既殯而祭。

translations.literal: Also examining the Rites—when a queen consort dies, the five seasonal sacrifices are not performed; after encoffinment sacrifices are performed.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites also state that when a queen consort dies, the five seasonal sacrifices cease until after encoffinment, when sacrifices resume.

sentences.zh: 所言五祀不行，則天地之祭不廢，遂議以園陵年月不便，須至變禮從宜。

translations.literal: What was said about the five sacrifices not being performed means the sacrifices to Heaven and Earth are not abolished; therefore it was debated that because the mausoleum dates were inconvenient, one must adapt the rites as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The suspension of the five sacrifices does not mean the rites to Heaven and Earth are abolished. Because the mausoleum schedule was inconvenient, they debated adapting the rites as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 又緣先准禮文，候神主升祔畢，方行享祀。

translations.literal: Also because according to prior approved ritual texts, one waits until the spirit tablet is elevated and enshrined before performing sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Prior ritual rulings also required waiting until the spirit tablet was enshrined before regular temple offerings could resume.

sentences.zh: 若俟丙午歲，則三年不祭宗廟，禮文有闕。

translations.literal: If one waits until the bingwu year, then for three years the ancestral temple would not be sacrificed to—the ritual canon would be deficient.
translations.idiomatic: If we wait until the bingwu year, the ancestral temple would go three years without sacrifice—a breach of ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 況明德皇太后德配先朝，禮合升祔。

translations.literal: Moreover, Empress Dowager Mingde's virtue matched the former reign—it is ritually fitting to elevate and enshrine her.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Empress Dowager Mingde's virtue matched that of the prior reign—enshrinement is ritually proper.

sentences.zh: 遂與史館檢討同共參詳，以為廟未祔則神靈不至，伏恐祭祀難行。

translations.literal: Thereupon together with the Historical Archives reviewers they jointly examined and considered that if the temple has not enshrined her, the spirit would not arrive—they feared sacrificial offerings would be hard to perform.
translations.idiomatic: They consulted with Historical Archives reviewers and concluded that without enshrinement the spirit would not be present—sacrifice would be impossible.

sentences.zh: 攢既畢則梓宮在郊，可以葬禮比附。

translations.literal: Once encoffinment is complete the imperial coffin is in the suburbs—it can be compared by analogy to burial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Once the temporary encoffinment is complete the imperial coffin rests in the suburbs—burial rites can be applied by analogy.

sentences.zh: 遂按《禮》云『葬者藏也，欲人不得而見也。』

translations.literal: Thereupon examining the Rites: 'Burial means concealment—wishing that people cannot see.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites define burial as concealment—keeping the deceased from sight.

sentences.zh: 既不欲穿壙動土，則龍輴、攢木、題湊，蒙槨上四柱如屋以覆，盡塗之。

translations.literal: Since one does not wish to dig a tomb and move earth, then the dragon hearse, encoffinment wood, inscribed panels, covered coffin with four pillars above like a roof to cover—all plastered over.
translations.idiomatic: Since we do not wish to open a tomb and disturb the earth, the dragon hearse, encoffinment frame, inscribed panels, and outer coffin are roofed over with four pillars like a house and sealed with plaster.

sentences.zh: 所合埋重，一依近例，便可升祔神主。

translations.literal: The suspended weight to be buried—all according to recent precedent—then the spirit tablet may be elevated and enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: The suspended weight should be buried according to recent precedent, and the spirit tablet may then be enshrined.

sentences.zh: 安易妄言，以凶仗為凶穢，目群官為顛倒，指梓宮為棺柩，令百司分析園陵，浼瀆聖聽，誣罔臣下。

translations.literal: Anyi spoke recklessly—calling mourning accoutrements impure mourning pollution, labeling the officials as inverted, pointing to the imperial coffin as a common coffin, ordering the hundred offices to analyze the mausoleum—defiling the sacred ear of the emperor, deceiving and misleading the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Anyi spoke recklessly. He called the mourning gear impure, accused the officials of reversing proper order, treated the imperial coffin as an ordinary coffin, and burdened every office with analyzing the mausoleum schedule—polluting the emperor's attention and deceiving his ministers.

sentences.zh: 安易又云：『昔日睹群官盡公，奉二帝諸后，並先山陵，後祔廟；

translations.literal: Anyi also said: 'In former days I saw the officials all correct in serving the two emperors and empresses—first the mountain tomb, then enshrinement in the temple;
translations.idiomatic: Anyi also said: 'Before, I saw officials handle things properly: for the two emperors and empresses, the mountain tomb came first and temple enshrinement second;

sentences.zh: 今日睹群官顛倒，奉明德皇太后，獨先祔廟，後園陵』者。

translations.literal: today I see the officials inverted in serving Empress Dowager Mingde—alone enshrining in the temple first and the mausoleum after.'
translations.idiomatic: today I see officials reversed: for Empress Dowager Mingde, temple enshrinement comes first and the mausoleum second.'

sentences.zh: 今詳當時先山陵後祔廟，正為年月便順，別無陰陽拘忌。

translations.literal: Now examining closely, at that time mountain tomb first and temple enshrinement after was precisely because the dates were convenient and smooth—there was no yin-yang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: On review, tomb before temple in those cases simply reflected convenient dates—nothing to do with yin-yang taboos.

sentences.zh: 今則年月未便，理合從宜。

translations.literal: Now the dates are inconvenient—it is logically fitting to adapt as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Now the dates are inconvenient—it is right to adapt the rites accordingly.

sentences.zh: 未埋重則禮文不備，未升祔則廟祭猶闕，須從變禮，以合聖情。

translations.literal: If the weight is not buried the ritual texts are incomplete; if not elevated and enshrined temple sacrifice is still lacking—one must follow adapted rites to accord with the sacred sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Without burying the suspended weight the rites remain incomplete; without enshrinement temple sacrifice cannot proceed. The rites must be adapted to match the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 兼明德皇太后將赴權攢，而安易所稱『柏城未焚凶仗，則凶穢唐突祖宗』，按《檀弓》云：『喪之朝也，順死者之孝心也。』

translations.literal: Moreover, Empress Dowager Mingde is about to proceed to temporary encoffinment, and what Anyi called 'if mourning accoutrements at Cypress City are not burned, then impurity affronts the ancestors'—examining the Tan Gong: 'The morning procession of mourning follows the deceased's filial heart.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as Empress Dowager Mingde prepares for temporary encoffinment, Anyi's claim that 'unburned mourning gear at Cypress City would impiously offend the ancestors' runs against the Tan Gong: 'The morning procession of mourning follows the deceased's filial devotion.'

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注云：『謂遷柩於廟。』

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary says: 'This means moving the coffin to the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary explains: 'This means moving the coffin to the temple.'

sentences.zh: 又云：『其哀離其室也，故至於祖考之廟而後行，商朝而殯于祖，周朝而遂葬。』

translations.literal: It also says: 'In their grief at leaving their chamber, therefore they first reach the temple of forefathers and then proceed—the Shang morning procession and encoffinment at the ancestor; the Zhou morning procession and then immediate burial.
translations.idiomatic: It adds: 'Mourners grieve to leave the chamber, so the procession goes first to the ancestral temple—the Shang held morning rites and encoffined at the ancestor; the Zhou held morning rites and proceeded straight to burial.'

sentences.zh: 今亦遙辭宗廟而後行，豈可以《禮經》所出目為顛倒，吉凶具儀謂之唐突哉？

translations.literal: Now also paying respects at the ancestral temple from afar and then proceeding—how can what the Ritual Canon prescribes be labeled inversion, and rites both auspicious and inauspicious fully observed be called impious affront?
translations.idiomatic: We too take leave of the ancestral temple before proceeding—how can ritual prescribed in the Canon be called inverted, or a procession with both mourning and honoring rites be called impious?

sentences.zh: 又云：『孝章皇后至道元年崩，亦緣有所嫌避，未赴園陵，出京權攢之時，不立神主入廟。

translations.literal: Also: 'Empress Xiaozhang died in the first year of Zhidao—also because of some taboo avoidance, not yet going to the mausoleum; when leaving the capital for temporary encoffinment, no spirit tablet was established in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: They also noted: 'Empress Xiaozhang died in the first year of Zhidao. Because of taboo constraints she had not yet reached the mausoleum. When her coffin left the capital for temporary encoffinment, no spirit tablet was installed in the temple.'

sentences.zh: 直至至道三年，西去園陵，禮畢，然後奉虞主還京，易神主祔廟，以合典禮。』

translations.literal: Only until the third year of Zhidao, going west to the mausoleum, after the rites were complete, then bearing the yu tablet back to the capital, exchanging for the spirit tablet and enshrining in the temple—to accord with canonical rites.'
translations.idiomatic: Not until the third year of Zhidao, after the western journey to the mausoleum and the completion of rites, was the yu tablet brought back to the capital, the spirit tablet installed, and enshrinement completed—exactly as canonical ritual required.'

sentences.zh: 今詳當時文籍，緣孝章為太宗嫂氏，上仙之時，止輟五日視朝，百官不曾成服，與今不同。

translations.literal: Now examining the documents of that time—because Xiaozhang was Taizong's sister-in-law, when she ascended to immortality only five days of court audience were suspended; the hundred officials never wore mourning garments—it differs from today.
translations.idiomatic: The records show that because Xiaozhang was Taizong's sister-in-law, when she died only five days of court were suspended and officials never donned full mourning—quite unlike the present case.

sentences.zh: 從初亦無詔命令住廟享。

translations.literal: From the beginning there was also no edict ordering suspension of temple offerings.
translations.idiomatic: From the outset no edict had suspended temple offerings either.

sentences.zh: 今明德皇太后母儀天下，主上孝極曾、顏，況上仙之初，即有遣命權停享祀。

translations.literal: Now Empress Dowager Mingde was the mother model of all under Heaven; the sovereign's filial piety reaches the level of Zeng and Yan; moreover at the beginning of her ascension to immortality there was already a dying decree provisionally suspending sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Mingde was mother to the realm. The emperor's filial piety equals that of Zengzi and Yan Hui. At her death an edict already suspended temple offerings temporarily.

sentences.zh: 今按禮文，固合如此。

translations.literal: Now examining the ritual texts—it is inherently fitting to be thus.
translations.idiomatic: By the ritual texts, this is entirely proper.

sentences.zh: 安易荒唐庸昧，妄有援引，以大功之親，比三年之制，欺罔君上，乃至於斯。

translations.literal: Anyi is absurd, vulgar, and ignorant—recklessly citing precedents, comparing a relative in dafu mourning to the three-year mourning regulation, deceiving and misleading the sovereign—going so far as this.
translations.idiomatic: Anyi is absurd and ignorant, citing precedents at random, comparing a dafu relative to three-year mourning, and deceiving his sovereign to this extent.

sentences.zh: 況安易以訐直自負，所詆者無非良善；

translations.literal: Moreover Anyi prides himself on blunt uprightness—those he slanders are none but the good and virtuous;
translations.idiomatic: Anyi prides himself on blunt honesty—yet those he attacks are always the good and upright;

sentences.zh: 以清要自高，所尚者無非鄙俗。

translations.literal: he holds himself high as pure and eminent—what he esteems is none but the vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: he poses as refined and principled—yet what he esteems is always the vulgar.

sentences.zh: 名宦之志，老而益堅；

translations.literal: Ambition for fame and office—growing stronger in old age;
translations.idiomatic: His hunger for rank and office only grew stronger with age;

sentences.zh: 詩書之文，懵而不習。

translations.literal: the texts of Poetry and Documents—obtuse and unstudied.
translations.idiomatic: while the classics of Poetry and Documents he barely knew at all.

sentences.zh: 本院所議，並明稱典故，旁考時宜，雖曰從權，粗亦稽古，請依無議施行。」

translations.literal: What this court has deliberated all clearly cites canonical precedents and consults contemporary appropriateness—though called adapting authority, it roughly also examines antiquity; we request implementation according to the deliberation without dispute."
translations.idiomatic: Our deliberations cite canonical precedents and weigh present circumstances. Though we adapt the rites, we have still examined antiquity. We ask that the plan proceed without further debate."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 安易又屢言陵廟事，詞多鄙俚。

translations.literal: Anyi again repeatedly spoke on tomb and temple affairs; his language was much coarse and vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: Anyi continued to speak repeatedly on tomb and temple affairs, his language crude and vulgar.

sentences.zh: 晚歲進趨不已，時論嗤之。

translations.literal: In his late years his pursuit of advancement did not cease; contemporary opinion scoffed at him.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he never stopped angling for promotion, and public opinion scorned him.

sentences.zh: 二年卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died, at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 錄其子承慶為國子博士，孫從政為太常寺奉禮郎。

translations.literal: His son Chengqing was enrolled as Erudite of the Directorate of Education; his grandson Congzheng as Gentleman for Ceremonies of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengqing was enrolled as an erudite of the Directorate of Education; his grandson Congzheng as a gentleman for ceremonies in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自古創業之君，其居潛舊臣，定策佐命，樹事建功，一代有一代之才，未嘗乏也。

translations.literal: The discourse says: From antiquity founding rulers and their old retainers from the time before ascension, who settled the plan and assisted in the mandate, established affairs and achieved merit—each age has the talent of its age; it has never been lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Founding emperors and the veteran ministers who served them before the throne, who shaped policy and helped secure the mandate, who built institutions and won achievements—in every age such talent has appeared; it has never been absent.

sentences.zh: 求其始終一心，休戚同體，貴為國卿，親若家相，若宋太祖之于趙普，可謂難矣。

translations.literal: Seek one of single heart from beginning to end, sharing weal and woe as one body, noble as a state minister yet intimate as a household chief minister—like Song Taizu toward Zhao Pu—this may be called difficult.
translations.idiomatic: To find one who served with a single heart from first to last, who shared triumph and trouble as one body, who was honored as a state minister yet trusted like a household counselor—as Taizu did with Zhao Pu—that is rare indeed.

sentences.zh: 陳橋之事，人謂普及太宗先知其謀，理勢或然。

translations.literal: In the affair of Chen Bridge, people say Pu and Taizong both knew the plan beforehand—the logic and momentum perhaps so.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Chen Bridge coup, many said both Pu and Taizong knew the plan in advance—a plausible reading of the logic and momentum.

sentences.zh: 事定之後，普以一樞密直學士立于新朝數年，范、王、魏三人罷相，始繼其位，太祖不亟于酬功，普不亟於得政。

translations.literal: After affairs were settled, Pu stood as a direct academy scholar of the Bureau of Military Affairs in the new dynasty for several years; Fan, Wang, and Wei three men left the chief ministership before he succeeded to the post—Taizu did not hasten to reward merit; Pu did not hasten to gain power.
translations.idiomatic: After the coup Pu served for years as a direct academy scholar of the Bureau of Military Affairs while Fan, Wang, and Wei in turn left the chief ministership—only then did he succeed them. Taizu did not rush to reward him; Pu did not rush to seize power.

sentences.zh: 及其當揆，獻可替否，惟義之從，未嘗以勳舊自伐。

translations.literal: When he came to hold the chief minister's seat, he offered assent and offered rejection—following only righteousness; he never vaunted himself as an old merit-holder.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became chief minister, he offered assent and dissent alike, following righteousness alone. He never traded on his founding merit.

sentences.zh: 偃武而修文，慎罰而薄斂，三百餘年之宏規，若平昔素定，一旦舉而措之。

translations.literal: Ceasing arms and cultivating culture, cautious in punishment and light in taxation—the grand design of more than three hundred years, as if settled in ordinary times, raised and set in place in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: He laid down arms and cultivated culture, kept punishments sparing and taxes light—the grand design that would sustain the dynasty for three centuries seemed already settled in his mind, ready to enact at once.

sentences.zh: 太原、幽州之役，終身以輕動為戒，後皆如其言。

translations.literal: In the campaigns of Taiyuan and Youzhou, throughout his life he took rash action as a warning; afterward all was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taiyuan and Youzhou campaigns he spent his life warning against rash military action—and later events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 家人見其斷國大議，閉門觀書，取決方冊，他日竊視，乃《魯論》耳。

translations.literal: The family saw him deciding great national deliberations, closing the door to read books, taking decisions from reference works—another day peeping secretly, it was only the Lu Discussions.
translations.idiomatic: His family watched him decide weighty affairs of state, then shut his door to read for guidance from his books—one day they peeked and found only the Analects.

sentences.zh: 昔傅說告商高宗曰：「學於古訓乃有獲，事不師古，以克永世，匪說攸聞。」

translations.literal: Formerly Fu Yue told Shang Gaozong: "Learning from ancient instruction brings gain; affairs not modeled on antiquity, to conquer and endure generations—this Fu Yue has not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yue once told King Gaozong of Shang: "Only by learning from the ancients can one gain wisdom. To govern for generations without heeding the past—of that I know nothing."

sentences.zh: 普為謀國元臣，乃能矜式往哲，蓍龜聖模，宋之為治，氣象醇正，茲豈無助乎。

translations.literal: Pu as the founding minister plotting for the state was able to take as model the sages of old, divining like tortoise and milfoil the sacred pattern—Song's governance, its atmosphere pure and upright—did this not also help?
translations.idiomatic: As the dynasty's founding strategist, Pu took the ancient sages as his model and divined the pattern of sage rule. The pure, upright cast of Song governance—surely he helped shape that.

sentences.zh: 晚年廷美、多遜之獄，大為太宗盛德之累，而普與有力焉。

translations.literal: In his later years the cases of Tingmei and Duoxun greatly became a burden on Taizong's abundant virtue—and Pu had a powerful hand in them.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the cases of Tingmei and Duoxun became a stain on Taizong's otherwise luminous reign—and Pu bore no small part in them.

sentences.zh: 豈其學力之有限而猶有患失之心歟？

translations.literal: Was it that his learning and strength were limited and he still had a heart that feared loss?
translations.idiomatic: Was his learning too shallow, and did fear of losing what he had still move him?

sentences.zh: 君子惜之。

translations.literal: Gentlemen regret this.
translations.idiomatic: Men of judgment lament it.
